summary: This note is an encyclopedia-style introduction to Venice, a city in northeastern Italy and capital of the Veneto region. It describes the city's location across 118 islands linked by 400 bridges in the Venetian Lagoon, its renowned beauty and UNESCO World Heritage status, and key administrative data such as area, population, and patron saint.
one_line: Venice is a northeastern Italian city and Veneto's capital, built across 118 lagoon islands linked by 400 bridges and listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
key_facts: Venice is a city in northeastern Italy and the capital of the Veneto region.
Venice is situated across a group of 118 small islands separated by canals.
The islands of Venice are linked by 400 bridges.
The islands are located in the shallow Venetian Lagoon, an enclosed bay.
The Venetian Lagoon lies between the mouths of the Po and the Piave rivers (more exactly between the Brenta and the Sile).
Parts of Venice are renowned for the beauty of their settings, their architecture, and artwork.
The lagoon and a part of the city are listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
Venice's total area is 414.57 km (160.07 sq mi).
Venice had a population of 260,897 in 2018.
Venice's population density is 630 per km (1,600 per sq mi).
The mayor of Venice is Luigi Brugnaro, who is independent.
Venice is in the metropolitan city of Venice (VE), with postal code 30100 and dialing code 041.
The patron saint of Venice is St. Mark the Evangelist, whose saint day is 25 April.
Venice's frazioni include Chirignago, Favaro Veneto, Mestre, Marghera, Murano, Burano, Giudecca, Lido, and Zelarino.
Venice uses Central European Time (UTC+1), with summer time at UTC+2.
